title: A variant's assumptions — lean-business capability
description: Formal shape of `<location>/<idea>/variants/<variant>/assumptions.yaml` (lean-business DEC-002 point 8): the variant's one list of assumptions, each with its id qualified by the variant, its statement as a leap of faith, where it comes from, its kind and its rank by risk. An assumption stores no outcome and no position: whether it is untested, being tested, supported, refuted or inconclusive follows from the experiments that test it (DEC-003 point 8). Its link to the canvas entry it comes from is no reference, since the method removes an entry its experiment refuted (DEC-002 point 7). The list is the namespace experiments reference, `[assumptions:<id>]`, which the core's data validation resolves among the lists it validates (COR-029). Companion per COR-018.

pkit_schema.description: The schema that binds this file (COR-023): `lean-business:assumptions`.

assumptions.description: The variant's assumptions, each with its `id` first.

id.description: The assumption's id, qualified by its variant, such as `meal-plan--direct--pays-monthly`.

statement.description: What the model takes for granted that no evidence supports yet, said as a leap of faith.

source.description: Where it comes from: an `entry` of the canvas, by its id, or an `input` of the estimate, by its name and its side where the model names several.

kind.description: The desk step whose risk it carries.

rank.description: Its rank by risk, the person's: 1 is the riskiest. A rank is no judgement an experiment rests on, so it takes no fingerprint.
